scenes.title: Egypt
scenes.subtitle: A history told only by its sources

scenes.caption: Photo 1850
scenes.text: Egypt, one of the world's oldest civilizations, was unified around 3150 BC by King Narmer.

scenes.caption: Photo 1850
scenes.text: It later came under Persian, Greek, Roman, and Arab rule before being joined to the Ottoman Empire in 1517.

scenes.caption: Photo 1850
scenes.text: Controlled by Britain in the late 19th century, it became a republic in 1953.

scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Cairo
scenes.text: Climate changes and/or overgrazing around 6000 BC began to desiccate the pastoral lands of Egypt, forming the Sahara.

scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Cairo
scenes.text: After an interval of independence, during which three indigenous dynasties reigned (the 28th, 29th and 30th dynasty), Artaxerxes III (358–338 BC) reconquered the Nile valley for a brief second period (343–332 BC), which is called…

scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Cairo
scenes.text: It fell to the Persians again in 343 BC after the last native Pharaoh, King Nectanebo II, was defeated in battle.

scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Cairo
scenes.text: The Byzantines were able to regain control of the country after a brief Persian invasion early in the 7th century, until 639–642, when Egypt was invaded and conquered by the Arab Islamic Empire.

scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Cairo
scenes.text: With the end of the Kurdish Ayyubid dynasty, the Mamluks, a Turco-Circassian military caste, took control about 1250.

scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Cairo
scenes.text: The mid-14th-century Black Death killed about 40% of the population of Egypt.

scenes.caption: Photo 1880 · Cairo
scenes.text: The Mamluks continued to govern the country until the conquest of Egypt by the Ottoman Turks in 1517, after which it became a province of the Ottoman Empire.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890
scenes.text: After the 15th century, the Ottoman invasion pushed the Egyptian system into decline.

scenes.caption: Photo 1890
scenes.text: The brief French invasion of Egypt led by Napoleon Bonaparte began in 1798.

scenes.caption: Photo 1883
scenes.text: Continued instability due to remaining British influence and increasing political involvement by the king led to the dissolution of the parliament in a military coup d'état known as the 1952 Revolution.

scenes.caption: Photo 1955
scenes.text: On 18 June 1953, the Egyptian Republic was declared, with General Muhammad Naguib as the first President of the Republic.

scenes.caption: Photo 1955
scenes.text: Nasser assumed power as president in June 1956.

scenes.caption: Photo 1955
scenes.text: On 24 June 2012, the election commission announced that Mohamed Morsi had won the election, making him the first democratically elected president of Egypt.

scenes.title: What the sources leave out
scenes.text: Between 650 and 1250, the sources consulted give no precise date.
